name: carddemo-ui
description: React 19 and TypeScript single-page application that replaces the AWS CardDemo 3270/BMS online screens with 21 browser routes.
//: STAGED FOUNDATION. This manifest is authored ahead of the ui tree it
describes, so the scripts below are the module's ENTRY CONTRACT rather than
a set of commands that all run at this checkpoint. Every file each script
names that is absent today is authored at a later index of the same
migration plan: tsconfig.json (typecheck, build), eslint.config.js (lint),
vite.config.ts (dev, build, preview), vitest.config.ts (test, test:watch),
.prettierrc (format, format:write), src/main.tsx and public/favicon.svg
(both referenced by index.html, which is Vite's build input). Present in
the tree now: index.html, tsconfig.node.json, .env.example and
src/messages/messages.ts. Consequently `npm ci` succeeds and installs the
pinned tree, and no other script can be expected to succeed yet. The
scripts and pins are declared now on purpose: the dependency set, the
compiler ceiling and the exact script names are decisions the later modules
must be written against, and retrofitting them after 21 screens exist is
how a tree ends up with two conflicting build entry points.
ENGINES: the floor is >=22.22.0 rather than the >=22.12.0 that the Vite and
Vitest chain asks for, because react-router 8.3.0 - a direct dependency -
itself declares engines.node >=22.22.0, the highest floor anywhere in
package-lock.json. Stating the lower number would let `npm ci` install a
tree whose own constraint the manifest understates, so the only warning
would come from npm's per-package EBADENGINE check rather than from the
project's own contract. Node 22.22.0 also satisfies every other declared
range in the lock, including the ^22.13.0 that eslint-plugin-jsdoc requires.

carddemoDependencyRationale.$note: Project-owned metadata that npm ignores. package.json is strict JSON and admits no comments, so the WHY that every other file in this tree carries as an inline comment lives here instead, keyed by the exact dependency entry it explains. Assumptions: each label key retains its trailing colon, so that the four canonical labels defined in docs/CODE_DOCUMENTATION_STANDARD.md appear here as exactly the literal, colon-terminated strings a fixed-string audit searches for. Dropping the colon because a JSON key is already delimited would produce a variant this repository does not accept. Trade-offs: only decisions that are NOT self-evident from the version string are recorded, because restating an obvious pin would bury the two that matter.

react-router.Alternatives Considered:: react-router-dom, which is the conventional choice and is deliberately ABSENT from this manifest. It has no release at major version 8 at all; its newest release is a thin re-export shim whose own dependency is react-router 7.18.1. Depending on it would therefore silently pin routing a full major version behind while looking like the safer, more idiomatic option. Every screen under ui/src/screens and ui/src/router.tsx import from react-router directly for this reason.
react-router.Assumptions:: the browser entry points this project needs -- BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Navigate, useNavigate, useParams and useSearchParams -- are all exported from react-router itself at 8.x, so the companion package adds no API. Reintroducing react-router-dom would not add capability; it would only add an indirection that caps the version.

typescript.Trade-offs:: held below the newest major release on purpose. typescript-eslint 8.65.0 peer-declares typescript ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0", so TypeScript 7.x falls outside the range the type-aware lint pass accepts. Crossing that bound does not fail loudly: it stops the type-aware pass, and with it the eslint-plugin-jsdoc documentation gate that enforces Rule 1 for this package, from running at all. Compile speed is therefore traded for a documentation gate that actually executes.
typescript.Assumptions:: this pin is load-bearing and is not routine version conservatism. Raising it requires first raising typescript-eslint to a release whose peer range admits the new compiler, and confirming that `npm run lint` still reports the JSDoc rules. Bumping typescript alone leaves the manifest installable and the gate silently inert.

typescript-eslint.Assumptions:: this entry is what imposes the TypeScript ceiling recorded above, so the two versions move together and neither may be raised alone. It supplies the type-aware rule set that eslint-plugin-jsdoc's contexts are evaluated against; without a compiler inside its peer range the JSDoc gate does not run.
